pages.text: "Red fruit!" Digging beneath the acacia shade, Tumba found a big pile. They lay over it. "All mine! I'll eat it all myself!"
Kiki and Moya approached. "Let us see, too!" Tumba pressed the fruit beneath their front hooves and turned away. "No! All mine!"
Sad, Kiki and Moya went to the waterhole. Tumba bit into a fruit alone. Sweet—but not fun at all. "Why doesn't it taste good?"
Moya returned with a yellow fruit and set it down. "Have half, Tumba. Eating alone was boring." Tumba lifted their head. "I... can have some?"
Tumba took a bite. "Tangy!" Moya glanced at the red pile. "What do yours taste like? Share half, taste two flavors!" Tumba pressed a red fruit with their snout and split it.
"This half's yours!" Tumba pushed it to Moya. "Sweet!" Moya said. Tumba ate yellow fruit. "Tangy!" Sweet and tangy—two flavors!
Tumba carried a red fruit to Kiki. "Half for you! Let's eat together!" Kiki received it in both paws. "Really? Thank you!" Share half, taste two flavors!
All three sat side by side in the shade, crunching with round cheeks. Tumba's tail popped up. "It tastes really good together!"
Now Tumba knew how to share. "One, ask 'Want to eat together?' Two, split in half! Three, yum together!" Next day, Tumba split a root. "Half for you, Moya!"
Moya nuzzled Tumba's side, and Kiki hugged their back. "You're the best!" Alone, one flavor. Sharing, two flavors. Share half, taste two flavors!
